to include a City Charter Amendment to move our local elections to November of odd-numbered years. This amendment will benefit the city by increasing voter turnout, reducing voter fatigue, and saving Dallas residents over $400,000.

In the dense areas near Downtown and Uptown, I would support a reduction of parking minimums to encourage more pedestrian and bicycle traffic. That approach would not be appropriate in less dense areas of the city, including most of District 11.
By attracting new businesses and growing the commercial tax base, the city can generate the needed funds to provide essential services while lowering the tax burden on residential property owners.
While open to thoughtful development in appropriate areas, Bill opposes the forced introduction of high-density housing into established residential zones.
Dallas must hold the line on increasing taxes with the goal of cutting taxes. Bill believes in cutting wasteful spending and conducting departmental audits.
Bill supports increasing the number of patrol police officers and ensuring our fire personnel are well-equipped to respond to emergencies.
He’ll focus on streamlining city services, prioritizing road and sidewalk repairs, modernizing traffic signals, and increasing transparency in how public works are executed.

He believes land use changes should be driven by community input, not top-down mandates, and will fight to ensure residents’ voices guide neighborhood planning, not bureaucrats or developers pushing unwanted density.
